tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Find companies by name (for example "netflix" or "planet fitness") among the subscriptions and memberships Postbye has a cancellation guide for. Returns each match's slug, category, how the company takes cancellations and the guide URL. Use the slug with get_cancellation_guide.

tools.name: get_cancellation_guide
tools.description: How to cancel one company's subscription or membership: how it takes cancellations, the notice period, the traps to check first, billing-partner notes, sources, when the facts were verified, the mailing address(es) on file and the guide and address page URLs. Accepts a company slug from search_compa

tools.name: get_cancellation_letter
tools.description: A plain-text cancellation letter for one company, built from the same template as Postbye's free letter tool, plus where to send it. Fields not supplied stay as [bracketed placeholders] to fill in. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: The category hubs of the cancellation guides (streaming, gyms, phone and internet, insurance and more) with the number of guides in each and the hub URL.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_companies, get_cancellation_guide, list_categories · Private data: get_cancellation_guide · Public sink: get_cancellation_letter.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_companies, get_cancellation_guide, list_categories · Private data: get_cancellation_guide · Public sink: get_cancellation_letter

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
